\begin{bankpassage}[id=TOPS03-P1-CHEM-S3-G5-6, source={TOPS - Test 03 (20 Nov 2022)}, questions={5-6}]
According to VSEPR theory electron pairs tend to minimize repulsions and these are in the order -- lone pair--lone pair $>$ lone pair--bond pair $>$ bond pair--bond pair. (Here bond pair refers to a single bond.) shapes of the molecules depend upon repulsions between bond pair and lone pair electrons.

The double bond is in need of more space as compared to the single bond. The repulsion order in relation to the bonds is as follow :

double bond--double bond $>$ double bond--single bond $>$ single bond--single bond

Keeping the central atom (having lone pair) same, if the electronegativity of the surrounding atom increases, the bond angle will decrease provided no other factors like size and back bonding play any role.

Keeping the surrounding atoms same, if the electronegativity of the central atom (having the lone pair) increases, the bond angle increases.
\end{bankpassage}

\begin{bankpassage}[id=STAR03-P2-CHEM-S3-G5-6, source={Star Review (Other) - Test 03 (04 Dec 2023)}, questions={5-6}]
The distribution of electrons among various molecular orbitals is called the electronic configuration of the molecule which provides us the following very important informations about the molecule.\par
\textbf{(A) Stability of molecule} : The molecule is stable if number of bonding molecular orbital electrons ($N_b$) is greater than the number of antibonding molecular orbital electrons ($N_a$).\par
\textbf{(B) Bond order} : Bond order $=(N_b-N_a)/2$\par
A positive bond order means a stable molecule while a negative or zero bond order means an unstable molecule.\par
\textbf{(C) Nature of bond} : Bond order $1$, $2$ or $3$ corresponds to single, double or triple bonds respectively.\par
\textbf{(D) Bond length :} Bond length decreases as bond order increases.\par
\textbf{(E) Magnetic nature} : Molecular orbitals in a molecule are doubly occupied, the substance is diamagnetic and it one or more molecular orbitals are singly occupied it is paramagnetic.
\end{bankpassage}
